title: Polynomial-bit constructive rounding candidate for matroid bases
reported_status: The supplied continuation reports a complete proof candidate for a deterministic polynomial-bit matroid-basis algorithm and a deterministic construction of an exactly unbiased rational output law. The report includes a proof narrative and source-reported finite diagnostics, but the linked standalone proof, ZIP, diagnostic code, and receipts were not supplied. No independent proof reconstruction, end-to-end implementation, scientific replay, or priority review was performed. Correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.
scientific_scope_status: For an arbitrary matroid on n elements accessed by an independence oracle, rational A∈Q^{m×n} with squared Euclidean column norms at most one, rational x in its base polytope, and rational objective c, the source claims a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm returning a basis B with cᵀ1_B≤cᵀx and ||A(1_B−x)||∞≤262336. For fixed A,x, an ellipsoid metarounding step is claimed to construct at most n+1 bases with rational probabilities, exact mean x, and the same discrepancy bound at every support point. The algorithmic claim is specific to matroid bases; it does not promote the broader N689 Boolean-polytope existence classification to an algorithm.
